long_biography.plain_text:
When Barry Zekelman inherited Atlas Tube with his brothers in 1986, the company was losing about $80,000 a month. At 19, he left university and concentrated on its machinery while experienced employees taught the young owners the tube business. Within eight months, a disciplined buying-and-selling formula produced their first profitable month.

Productivity became a lasting operating method. Zekelman introduced gain-sharing, linking higher pay to employee ideas that increased output. A later combination with John Maneely created a broader tube group, and he remained in management through its private-equity ownership. His family bought back Carlyle's majority interest in 2011; he remains executive chairman and chief executive.
